summary: Do not ship: skill-scoped clarification can split episode state across two directories and bind a generated plan to the wrong workflow.

findings.title: Subdirectory sessions create conflicting root and nested episode identities
findings.body: When invoked with `--workflow`, the recorder uses the raw payload cwd instead of walking to the governed root. In a governed project opened from a subdirectory, the plugin-wide registration writes the root episode and may infer workflow `work`, while the skill-scoped registration writes a second nested episode with the correct workflow. The clarification guard accepts the nested record, but `approved-artifact-persist` resolves to the project root and uses the root episode's workflow as planning evidence. It can therefore bind a `/dev`, `/ds`, or other generated plan as `work`, causing workflow substitution, conflicting receipts, or later admission failures. This follows directly from the two registrations using different roots.
findings.recommendation: For the skill-scoped path, use `governedRoot(start) ?? start` so both registrations target the same governed root. Add an integration test invoking both registrations from a nested directory and assert that only the root episode exists, carries the skill workflow, and drives plan persistence with that same identity.
